Koppies Kill Zone

By: Anina Peens | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A deadly stretch of the N1 hides in plain sight — where broken drainage, unanswered emails, and official silence have turned a road into a graveyard.

Unique Selling Point:
You may have driven this road without ever knowing — it’s one of the most dangerous stretches in the country. Crumbling, unmarked, and ignored for over a decade, it’s claimed dozens of lives while those in power do nothing

Summary:
Tucked in the heart of the Free State, the Koppies offramp seems unremarkable—until you count the bodies. Carte Blanche investigates why this deadly stretch of the N1 continues to claim lives, despite repeated warnings to every authority responsible for fixing it.

Further information:
In the middle of South Africa’s silo and farm country, on a quiet stretch of the N1 between Sasolburg and Kroonstad, lies an offramp that has become one of the most dangerous pieces of road in the country. The Koppies offramp seems ordinary—surrounded by maize fields, cattle fences, and wide Free State skies. But during heavy rain, this road turns deadly. Stormwater gushes across the highway, vehicles lose control, and people die. Again and again.
During rainstorms, water barrels across the tarmac from poorly managed culverts, turning the highway into a skid trap. Vehicles aquaplane. Lives are lost—repeatedly. For years, engineers, farmers, and families have raised the alarm. The first emails were sent more than a decade ago. But nothing has changed.
A tender to fix the road was awarded—then cancelled. A ministerial report was ordered—then never released. The local municipality shrugs. SANRAL passes the buck. RTMC doesn’t respond. The mayor of the region has held two public prayer days on this road. Yet no one has fixed the drainage, installed warning signs, or held anyone accountable.
So how many more deaths will it take? How does someone in authority ignore email after email, and still sleep at night? As journalists, we are not engineers. We cannot rebuild roads. But what we can do is warn the public, if the very agencies created to do that won’t.
Through the voices of those who have lost the most—like Candice Dunn, who lost her husband and two young children—we tell the story of a silent disaster, unfolding in plain sight, on a road we all drive.

Press Release:


Koppies Kill Zone
It looks like a perfectly ordinary stretch of the N1 between Johannesburg and Kroonstad. But when it rains, this piece of highway turns into a death trap on which dozens of lives have been lost. The reason? Questionable drainage, a complete lack of warning signs – and official silence. As families endure unimaginable tragedy, what will it take to stop the disaster unfolding in plain sight?
Producer & Presenter: Anina Peens

Script:


­KOPPIES KILL ZONE: DRAFT SCRIPT 2

Andre van Zyl: “Ja ons het omtrent tot hier gekom. Ek skat ons is nou so 150 meter van die brug af”
SUBS: yes we came to about here. I’m guessing we were about 150 metres from the bridge…
Andre van Zyl: Gesien daar lê ‘n kar op sy sy.”
SUBS: We saw a car lying on its side.
Andre van Zyl: Ons was omtrent hier gewees toe sê ek vir haar hier lê ‘n kind in die pad.

Andre van Zyl: “Hy het hier gelê onder die brug”
Ilse van Zyl: Hy is van die brug af en hy het daar gelê met sy gesiggie op die grond…
SUBS; He was lying here under the bridge. He came off the bridge and lay there with his little face on the ground
VO
A bridge in the Free State… under which lie the twisted wrecks of cars… silent evidence of catastrophe.
BEAT
VO
Above us, one of the busiest highways in the country, the N1…Between Johannesburg and Kroonstad.
The debris is all too familiar to Andre van Zyl and his wife Ilse, who own the farm through which this part of the highway runs.
UPSOUND ILSE: “Ons het §hom uit die water uit geskuif, hiernatoe.”
SUBS: We moved him out of the water, to here.
Andre van Zyl: “Hierdie ring is die Fortuner se ring wat om sy lyfie was…”
SUBS: This ring is the Fortuner’s ring that was around his little body…

VO
Now, months later, no longer the mangled remains of a deadly crash… the twisted steel has become a memorial to unimaginable trauma.
FADE TO BL
CANDICE DUNN
We had spent the most incredible time together.
VO
It had been a good holiday in the Eastern Cape for Candice Dunn, her husband Andrew and their two young children, Gemma and Matthew.
CANDICE DUNN
We go there every December. It's my father-in-law and my mother-in-law's farms that we go to.
VO
The family was excited to start renovations of their home in Johannesburg at the start of the new year, so Candice headed home a few days early.


CANDICE DUNN
It's the first time that we have actually gone on holiday in separate cars. I changed the plans in terms of coming back to earlier to make sure that on the six, when the builders had arrived, that everything was in order.

VO
But the day the renovations started – as Andrew and the children headed home – life changed forever.


CANDICE DUNN
I spoke to my family half an hour before and Andrew said, Candice, it's raining. And I said, please, just please just be careful. And it was the most he was the most careful, most vigilant driver.
VO
But as Andrew crossed the bridge over the Van Zyls’ farm, his car hit water that had pooled on the road in the heavy rain.
[BREATH]
Andre van Zyl: Toe ek hom sien en hy lyk soos ‘n klein rugbyspelertjie het ek dadelik vir haar gese, hoor hier, al is hy dood, kom ons bid vir hom.
When I saw him and he looked like a little rugby player, I immediately said to her, listen here, even if he’s dead, let’s pray for him
VO
Andre and Ilse were first to arrive at the scene. The SUV carrying Candice’s family had aquaplaned, its tires losing contact with the road.

Out of control, it spun into oncoming traffic, and collided head-on with a vehicle travelling in the opposite direction.

Candice’s son Matthew was flung from the back window and over the bridge, where he lay as water cascaded from the road above.

Andre van Zyl: Sy crayons en sy goed het hier afgespoel en sy se toe vir my sy gaan…
Ilse van Zyl: Ek gaan hom skuif, want dit lyk of hy begin lig
SUBS: His crayons and things had washed away here, and she said to me, I’m going…
I’m going to move him, because it looks like he’s starting to float.
VO
Meanwhile, emergency services arrived at the scene above.
CANDICE DUNN
I was screaming and I said, where is my family? He's my family. She said, hold on to put me on the phone to a man. And I was screaming and I said, we're here, who are you. And I said, I'm the wife and I'm the mother. And he said, I can't do this. Pass the phone back to the lady. And I realized something was wrong and I'd fallen to the floor. I said. How many? She said, have you got someone around? I said how many.. how many? And she said, all of them
BEAT

VO
As André walked up to the bridge, another car lost control in the rain.

Andre van Zyl: Terwyl ek daar bo gestaan het het daar nog ‘n ongeluk gebeur, ook ‘n bakkie wat gegly het en daai bakkie het baie skade gekry, die stroom water wat oor die pad geloop is net te veel.
SUBS: While I was standing up there, another accident happened — also a bakkie that slipped — and that bakkie was badly damaged. The stream of water flowing across the road was just too much.”
VO
During the past festive season alone, 25 people died on this stretch of road – two percent of all fatal crashes in the country. All on a single section of highway a few kilometres long.

BEAT
VO

When it rains, aquaplaning here isn’t just likely—it’s almost inevitable.

But most accidents here occur in dry conditions – at least, according to the National Roads Agency, SANRAL. It’s responsible for our national highways.

LOUW KANNEMEYER
What seems to be happening is the drivers are picking up excessive speed to pass vehicles in that 2km section.

VO
Louw Kannemeyer is one of Sanral’s senior engineers.

LOUW KANNEMEYER
So, in the December period, on the 1st of December we had a fatal accident, a head-on collision in dry conditions. Unsafe overtaking at high speed, two fatalities. On the 8th of December we had the awful accident where a taxi drove into the back of a broken down truck - dry, clear conditions. So, once again there’s no water related.
Anina Peens: But there’s a structural issue on this part of the road, that’s what I’m trying to get at. When it rains, the water doesn't drain.
Louw: So, in terms of, when we specifically look at aquaplaning… So it’s important to know that we in detail measure the condition of our network. We use highly sophisticated survey vehicles that are equipped with lasers, 3D cameras, that enables us to measure the surface in great detail. Based on those results there is no risk.

CANDICE DUNN
There’s been a multitude of accidents driving on that bridge. And exactly what had happened to Andrew in terms of aquaplaning hitting the barrier, the car spinning,
And there is enough evidence to show there is drainage issues. The road is slippery. Farmers can tell you this.
VO

André is often on hand to help drivers who lose control and aquaplane through the barriers and fences onto his land. And he thinks he knows what’s causing the problem.
ANDRE VAN ZYL
My opinie is, hierdie voor wat die water wegvoer kom ‘n paar honderd meter van bo af wat die water wegvoer. En dan is hierdie afvoer sloot veronderstel ek is gemaak om water weg te keer van die brug af, maar hy is ooit verbind nie, die water gaan mos nou nie opdraand loop en oorspring nie? Ek dink dit is net nie klaargemaak nie. Of dit dalk ‘n ontwerpsfout ek weet nie.
In my opinion, this drain that’s supposed to carry the water away starts a few hundred meters further up. And then there’s this trench here, which I assume was made to divert water away from the bridge — but it was never connected properly. Water obviously isn’t going to flow uphill or jump across. I just don’t think it was ever completed. Or maybe it’s a design flaw, I don’t know.
VO
So instead of draining the water away, the road’s design seems to make it flow over the surface, and under the wheels of passing vehicles.

ANDRE VAN ZYL
Andre: hy begin so kilometer terug, die padoppervlak se water kom hier af. Hierdie sloot loop vol
Anina: so hierdie is soos ‘n rivier wat hier afkom
Andre: en daar waar ilse nou loop, vir een of ander rede gaan die water oor die pad.
Anina: stoot hy soontoe.
Andre: vir een of ander rede stoot die water oor die pad. En dit is waar die mense begin gly.
Die stroom is ‘n sterk stroom want dit moet n sterk stroom wees om ‘n kar op te te tel en hom te draai.

VO
That’s exactly what happens: the water lifts your car off the road, as we experienced at an advanced driving centre.

UPSOUND
GO PRO
09:49:05:25
Matthew: You need to go in with a lot of speed.
Anina: And then turn?
Matthew: Ja, go, go, go!
SOURCE: 093410V1
09:49:27:19
Anina: How fast was I driving?
Mat: not very
Anina: 60km not even
Mat: 40/50
Anina: So this can literally happen at a lower speed?

VO
It doesn’t matter how careful you are—whether you’re sticking to the speed limit, driving a heavy, high-tech car, or even have brand new tyres. If water hits your wheels at just the right angle and speed, the car is lifted off the road. The tyres lose grip. Most people instinctively brake or turn—and that’s when the front wheels lock, the rear wheels spin, and the car rotates.
PAUSE
VO
Driven by her insufferable loss, Candace is determined to put this stretch of the N1 under the spotlight, pushing for accountability.
CANDICE DUNN
Highway horror… ten die in N1 crash. Taxi accident leaves 5 dead, 8 injured. Two people killed, multiple injured in two seperate collisions on the N1 Free State. N1 close to Koppies. If you look at every single one of these that I have looked at. Here, here we go again. It dates back to 2021, this one. Trucker burns to death, another seriously injured. N1 Koppies crash.
VO
Despite all these reports, SANRAL maintains that their data paints a different picture.

LOUW KANNEMEYER
It is not a road where in terms of accidents it is in one of the top 20 corridors in the country.
I think you need to appreciate,if we just respond and manage the network based on what is reported in the media we won’t be able to effectively manage The network.
Anina Peens: Sure, but this has been a problem for over 20 years.
Louw: It’s not been a problem for over 20 years, so once again I think accusations are being made which is very easy to do based on hearsay, based on eyewitness accounts.
Anina Peens: But they are the people on the ground. I mean, they are there.
Louw: yes, they’re on that road.
Anina Peens: That is the road we’re talking about.
Louw: Yes.
Anina Peens; we’re not talking about other roads now. We want to know what is being done about that road.
Louw: So, so what we’re saying to you; in relation to other roads in the country, what they report there is no worse than any other roads, and there are actually roads worse than that. So based on our asset management system we did identify the need for a periodic maintenance action on the section from kilometre zero to 29, which is up to the Koppies.
VO
But an independent civil engineer we consulted agreed that stretch of road has drainage issues which must be investigated.
Routine maintenance is only scheduled to begin in 2026.


BREATH
VO
That’s little comfort to Candice. All she has left is the accident’s only survivor: the dog little Matthew got for Christmas.
CANDICE
I don’t want to carry on but I do this for them… I do this for them. I want accountability. This is not about me. It’s never been about me and what’s going on in my mind. It’s about them… It’s about justice.


END

And then there’s this trench here, which I assume was made to divert water away from the bridge — but it was never connected properly. Water obviously isn’t going to flow uphill or jump across. Hierdie sloot loop vol Anina: so hierdie is soos ‘n rivier wat hier afkom Andre: en daar waar ilse nou loop, vir een of ander rede gaan die water oor die pad. Anina: stoot hy soontoe. VO That’s exactly what happens: the water lifts your car off the road, as we experienced at an advanced driving centre. UPSOUND GO PRO 09:49:05:25 Matthew: You need to go in with a lot of speed. Anina: And then turn? Matthew: Ja, go, go, go! SOURCE: 093410V1 09:49:27:19 Anina: How fast was I driving? Mat: not very Anina: 60km not even Mat: 40/50 Anina: So this can literally happen at a lower speed? If water hits your wheels at just the right angle and speed, the car is lifted off the road. The tyres lose grip. Most people instinctively brake or turn—and that’s when the front wheels lock, the rear wheels spin, and the car rotates. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A deadly stretch of the N1 hides in plain sight — where broken drainage, unanswered emails, and official silence have turned a road into a graveyard.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: You may have driven this road without ever knowing — it’s one of the most dangerous stretches in the country. Crumbling, unmarked, and ignored for over a decade, it’s claimed dozens of lives while those in power do nothing
metadata.Summary: Tucked in the heart of the Free State, the Koppies offramp seems unremarkable—until you count the bodies. Carte Blanche investigates why this deadly stretch of the N1 continues to claim lives, despite repeated warnings to every authority responsible for fixing it.
metadata.Further information: In the middle of South Africa’s silo and farm country, on a quiet stretch of the N1 between Sasolburg and Kroonstad, lies an offramp that has become one of the most dangerous pieces of road in the country. The Koppies offramp seems ordinary—surrounded by maize fields, cattle fences, and wide Free State skies. But during heavy rain, this road turns deadly. Stormwater gushes across the highway, vehicles lose control, and people die. Again and again. During rainstorms, water barrels across the tarmac from poorly managed culverts, turning the highway into a skid trap. Vehicles aquaplane. Lives are lost—repeatedly. For years, engineers, farmers, and families have raised the alarm. The first emails were sent more than a decade ago. But nothing has changed. A tender to fix the road was awarded—then cancelled. A ministerial report was ordered—then never released. The local municipality shrugs. SANRAL passes the buck. RTMC doesn’t respond. The mayor of the region has held two public prayer days on this road. Yet no one has fixed the drainage, installed warning signs, or held anyone accountable. So how many more deaths will it take? How does someone in authority ignore email after email, and still sleep at night? As journalists, we are not engineers. We cannot rebuild roads. But what we can do is warn the public, if the very agencies created to do that won’t. Through the voices of those who have lost the most—like Candice Dunn, who lost her husband and two young children—we tell the story of a silent disaster, unfolding in plain sight, on a road we all drive.
metadata.Reason for legal: Someone needs to take responsibility whether it's the road traffic management corporation or the minister of transport... but we will start with the local municipality and work our way up until we get answers.
metadata.Reason for graphics: To explain to the viewer where the road lies.
